_instructions.note: Edit prompts here manually. The system_prompt is sent as the system message. Each case has a user_prompt_template where {disease}, {inputs_block}, and {metamodel} are filled in at runtime. The inputs_block is assembled from whichever input sections are available for that case. Output should be XML following the metamodel format.

system_prompt: You are an expert in mathematical epidemiology and compartmental disease modelling. Your task is to extract a structured epidemiological model from scientific paper content. Follow the metamodel exactly and return valid XML matching the compartmental metamodel format. No explanations, no markdown code blocks, no text before or after. Begin directly with the XML.

output_format.description: All cases return XML following the metamodel format. Use the XML schema and element names from the metamodel. Use compartment indices in format '//@comparments.X' for flow targets.

flows.rateParameter: string — reference //@parameters.X instead of numeric rate

attributes.name: string — symbol as in paper e.g. 'γ', 'β₂', 'μₕ'

C01.name: baseline
C01.user_prompt_template:
You are given the full text of a scientific paper describing an epidemiological model for {disease}.

{inputs_block}

=== METAMODEL ===
{metamodel}

=== YOUR TASK ===
Using ONLY the full paper text provided above, extract the complete compartmental epidemiological model.

Extract:
1. All compartments (state variables). Use full descriptive names. If the model is stratified (e.g. by age or population group), include every stratum as a separate compartment with both primary and secondary names.
2. All flows (transitions) between compartments, including transmission flows (ContactFlow), progression and recovery flows (RateFlow), recruitment and birth flows (BirthSource), and death flows (DeathSink).
3. All parameters with their symbols, values (if given), units, and descriptions.

Follow the metamodel strictly for flow types and naming conventions. Return the result as valid XML matching the compartmental metamodel format.

C04.name: grobid_images
C04.user_prompt_template:
You are given two inputs for a scientific paper describing an epidemiological model for {disease}:
1. Structured paper sections extracted by GROBID (core technical sections only, intro and conclusion removed)
2. Descriptions of figures extracted from the paper

{inputs_block}

=== METAMODEL ===
{metamodel}

=== YOUR TASK ===
Using the structured sections for model equations and description, and the figure descriptions for visual model structure (compartment diagrams, flow diagrams), extract the complete compartmental epidemiological model.

Extract:
1. All compartments (state variables). Use full descriptive names. Cross-reference text and figure descriptions — figures often reveal stratifications or compartments not clearly described in text. If the model is stratified, include every stratum as a separate compartment.
2. All flows (transitions) between compartments. Flow diagrams in figures are especially useful for identifying ContactFlow vs RateFlow and direction.
3. All parameters with their symbols, values (if given), units, and descriptions.

Follow the metamodel strictly for flow types and naming conventions. Return the result as valid XML matching the compartmental metamodel format.

C05.name: grobid_equations
C05.user_prompt_template:
You are given two inputs for a scientific paper describing an epidemiological model for {disease}:
1. Structured paper sections extracted by GROBID (core technical sections only, intro and conclusion removed)
2. The model equations in LaTeX format

{inputs_block}

=== METAMODEL ===
{metamodel}

=== YOUR TASK ===
Using the structured sections for context and the equations as the primary source of model structure, extract the complete compartmental epidemiological model.

The equations are your most reliable source. Each differential equation corresponds to one compartment. Each term on the right-hand side corresponds to one flow — positive terms are inflows, negative terms are outflows. Parameter symbols appear directly in the equations.

Extract:
1. All compartments — one per differential equation. Use full descriptive names from the text, not just the variable letter.
2. All flows — derive directly from equation terms. Identify ContactFlow (terms involving a product of two compartment variables) vs RateFlow (terms involving only one compartment variable).
3. All parameters — extract every symbol that appears in the equations. Match to descriptions and values in the text sections.

Follow the metamodel strictly for flow types and naming conventions. Return the result as valid XML matching the compartmental metamodel format.

C10.name: fulltext_tables

{inputs_block}

{metamodel}

C11.name: everything
C11.user_prompt_template:
You are given the complete set of available inputs for a scientific paper describing an epidemiological model for {disease}:
1. The full raw paper text
2. Structured paper sections extracted by GROBID
3. Parameter tables extracted by Camelot
4. Descriptions of figures extracted from the paper
5. The model equations in LaTeX format

{inputs_block}

=== METAMODEL ===
{metamodel}

=== YOUR TASK ===
Using all available inputs, extract the most complete and faithful compartmental epidemiological model possible. When inputs conflict, use this priority order: equations > tables > GROBID sections > full text > figures.

Extract:
1. All compartments — equations and figures are the most reliable sources for the complete list. Use text for full descriptive names. Include every stratum if the model is stratified.
2. All flows — equations define them precisely (each term = one flow). Figures confirm direction and topology. Include every flow, including demographic flows (births, deaths) if present.
3. All parameters — tables give the most reliable values and units. Equations give symbols. Text gives descriptions. Include every parameter that appears in any input.

Follow the metamodel strictly for flow types and naming conventions. Return the result as valid XML matching the compartmental metamodel format.
